clue.text: Not all children own up for honour's sake

indicators.note: only part of the run of words is used, so the answer sits inside them

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the whole of the second

explanation.surface: Children are urged to confess to their misdeeds for the sake of their good name.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans childREN OWN; 'own up' reads as one phrase, but only 'own' is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown is fame and high public esteem, which is one established sense of the word honour.

clue.text: A horseless carriage

blocks.note: surface reading: the old name for an early motor car
setter's reading: a carriage with no horse because a man pulls it

explanation.walkthrough: Horseless carriage was the Victorian name for the motor car, which is what the solver first reaches for.
explanation.definitionFit: This light two-wheeled vehicle is drawn by a person on foot, so it is a carriage needing no horse.

clue.text: Sisters collectively giving pigeon to poet

blocks.note: the nun is a fancy breed of pigeon with a hood of feathers
Thomas Hood, the nineteenth-century English poet

explanation.surface: A group of sisters hand over a pet pigeon to a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Nunhood names the state of being nuns, and by extension the religious sisters as a body.

clue.text: Mathematicians in dispute

blocks.note: first meaning: Cambridge graduates with first-class honours in mathematics
second meaning: people who argue noisily

explanation.surface: Mathematicians are having an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: At Cambridge University the students placed in the first class of the mathematics exams are called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both Cambridge maths firsts and people who quarrel at length.

clue.text: Scattered thus to arrest old highwayman holding the gold

indicators.note: to arrest someone is to take them in, so one word holds the next inside it
holding something means keeping it inside, so the highwayman word wraps the gold

an archaic word for a highwayman, as in footpad
the heraldic word for gold

explanation.walkthrough: Footpad was the old word for a robber on foot, and in heraldry gold is called or; one container sits inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic means occurring at irregular, isolated intervals, which is what scattered describes here.

clue.text: Report the problem when aiming for a 20

blocks.note: a report is a bang, as of a gun
taken as written
a problem to be solved

explanation.walkthrough: 20 refers to 20-across, MATCH, here in its sense of a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose marriage is what a suitor does when seeking a wedding with someone.

clue.text: Don possibly cuts Mexican artist

blocks.note: Diego Rivera, the Mexican muralist

explanation.surface: A university don slashes a painting by a Mexican artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a university lecturer, but the Don is a river in Russia and in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The Don is a well-known example of a watercourse, so 'possibly' marks it as one instance.

clue.text: Certificate awarded to endlessly discreet person

indicators.note: without an end, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: a tactful person

explanation.definitionFit: A diploma is a document issued by a college certifying that a course has been completed.

clue.text: Time policemen turned up to identify this poison!

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
the Royal Ulster Constabulary, the Northern Ireland police force until 2001

explanation.surface: Detectives arrive in time to identify the poison used in a murder.
explanation.definitionFit: Curare is a plant extract used by South American hunters to tip arrows, a paralysing poison.

clue.text: Financially secure like some old ships

blocks.note: first meaning: thoroughly reliable, especially as an investment
second meaning: with hulls sheathed in copper

explanation.surface: Old ships are a sound financial investment.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailing ships had copper plates on their hulls to resist worm and weed, so the word came to mean dependable.

clue.text: Fruity part of poem about a student at university?

definitions.note: adjective standing for the noun, a kind of fruit

indicators.note: about means around, so the poem part goes around the next letters

blocks.note: a canto is a division of a long poem
taken as written
L for learner, the plate on a learner driver's car
a student in residence at Oxford or Cambridge is said to be up

explanation.surface: A student at college reads part of a fruity, risqué poem.
explanation.walkthrough: A student is said to be up while in residence at Oxford or Cambridge. The question mark admits that 'Fruity' stretches to define a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantaloup is a variety of melon with orange flesh, so the setter calls it fruity in a playful way.

clue.text: Notable king - a treacherous type

blocks.note: a very important person
Latin rex shortened, as in a royal cipher

explanation.surface: A famous monarch turns out to be a traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Viper is a common figurative term for a spiteful, treacherous person, from the venomous snake.

clue.text: Put up rent as a temporary expedient

blocks.note: to put up at an inn is to stop or stay there
a rent is a tear or opening

explanation.surface: A landlord raises the rent as a short-term fix for money troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord, but here it is a tear, the noun from rend.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is something used for the moment until a proper replacement is found, exactly a makeshift measure.

clue.text: Provide refuge for nurse

blocks.note: first meaning: shelter or hide someone
second meaning: keep a feeling alive in the mind, as with a grudge

explanation.surface: Someone takes in a nurse who needs a place to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb means to give shelter, and in its other sense one keeps a grudge or hope in mind, just as one nurses it.

clue.text: Empty seat left by son

indicators.note: something left by a person has been abandoned, so that letter goes away

blocks.note: a saddle is a rider's seat
the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son walks off, leaving his chair vacant.
explanation.walkthrough: The S at the front of SADDLE is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: As an old adjective, addle means idle or barren, as in addle-pated or an addle egg that yields nothing.

clue.text: Compensation left in old Spanish coin

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

blocks.note: the real was a silver coin of Spain
quit is a past tense meaning departed

explanation.surface: Someone is paid off with a single old Spanish coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like L, the usual abbreviation, but here it means departed.
explanation.definitionFit: Requital is repayment or return for something received, whether reward or revenge, so compensation fits.

clue.text: One thousand ways they outwardly display impudence

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
the Roman numeral for a thousand
modes are ways or methods
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A thousand different ways people show cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Immodesty can mean boldness or forwardness, a lack of becoming restraint, which is a form of impudence.

clue.text: New shop-boy (or girl, say) serving us with gas

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a first name used for both men and women

explanation.surface: A new shop assistant serves customers with gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Phosgene is a choking poison gas, carbonyl chloride, used in the First World War.

clue.text: Hoses are laid out in the Strand

indicators.note: laying things out arranges them afresh, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Fire hoses are unrolled along the Strand, the famous London street.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital S makes it the London street, but strand is also an old word for a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand is the land at the edge of the sea or a lake, a literary synonym for a beach.

clue.text: Closely inspect grill

blocks.note: first meaning: look at carefully
second meaning: question someone hard

explanation.surface: Someone checks a grill pan carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both scrutinise and interrogate, as a lawyer questions a witness in court.

clue.text: Correspond with union

blocks.note: first meaning: agree with or be equal to
second meaning: a marriage

explanation.surface: Someone writes letters to a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correspond' suggests letter-writing, but it means agree.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means agree or tally with, and as a noun it is a marriage or pairing of two people.

clue.text: A philosopher found order in this? Exactly

indicators.note: the order is found in the word, that is, sitting inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
the Order of Merit, a British honour
from to a T, meaning exactly

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a philosopher could find order in this, and is told yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thomist is a follower of the philosophy of St Thomas Aquinas, so one kind of philosopher.

clue.text: Passionate student in a 1 ac

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the following word

blocks.note: taken as written
L for learner
the answer to 1 across, replaced by a synonym

explanation.surface: A student caught up in the glare of celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 ac means the answer to 1 across, RENOWN; its synonym FAME takes the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Aflame describes burning with strong feeling, which is how a passionate person is figuratively pictured.

clue.text: The father we say should be charged

indicators.note: what we say is speech, so the word is wanted for its spoken form

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
a word for should, matched by an old word for anything

explanation.surface: The priest, it is agreed, ought to face criminal charges.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraught means laden or filled, as a situation can be fraught with or charged with tension.

clue.text: It's a grind for Guildhall's first architect

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: the initial letter of the name
John Nash, the Regency architect of Regent Street

explanation.surface: Designing the Guildhall was hard work for its first architect.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guildhall is the City of London's civic hall. 'A grind' looks like a slog, but the word is a verb for grinding teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: To gnash is to grind the teeth together, usually in anger or despair.

clue.text: Boring outside broadcast

indicators.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so the letters are flung into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A dull TV programme made on location.
explanation.walkthrough: An outside broadcast is a television programme filmed away from the studio, which hides the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedious describes something wearisome and dull, a direct synonym for boring.

clue.text: Inner personality of a Manx cat, possibly?

indicators.note: the Manx breed of cat has no tail, so the final letter is missing

blocks.note: a cat is one example

explanation.surface: Wondering about the inner life of a tailless cat from the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: Manx cats come from the Isle of Man and are born without tails, so the word loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jung's psychology the anima is the inner self or soul, the part of the psyche turned inward.

clue.text: Unrealistic ideas retailed by runners?

blocks.note: first meaning: foolish or fanciful talk
second meaning: illicit liquor sold by smugglers and bootleggers

explanation.surface: Athletes peddle impractical schemes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runners' suggests athletes, but rum-runners and bootleggers smuggled spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both nonsense and illegally distilled whisky, the kind of thing smugglers sold.

clue.text: Form of protection one's pupils are under

clue.text: Trouble encountered in wood when returning shrub
